prompt: Which two checks confirm the switch-side data/voice configuration of a port? Choose two.
options: Check only that the port is administratively configured as access
Verify that both configured VLANs exist and are active
Treat successful PC data traffic as proof of voice registration
Read the port’s access VLAN and voice VLAN settings
Require the phone port to negotiate a general-purpose trunk
explanation: Check that both VLANs exist and are active, and read the port’s actual access and voice VLAN settings. Phone power, provisioning and registration need their own checks.

whyWrong.0: Access mode alone does not show that the intended VLANs are active.
whyWrong.2: PC traffic does not verify voice addressing or registration.
whyWrong.4: Access-plus-voice does not need a general trunk.

prompt: Which command directly displays a port’s administrative mode, operational mode, access VLAN and voice VLAN?
options: `show mac address-table interface fastethernet0/1`
`show interfaces fastethernet0/1 switchport`
`show ip interface brief`
`show power inline`
explanation: `show interfaces <port> switchport` shows administrative mode, operational mode, access VLAN and voice VLAN together.

whyWrong.0: The MAC table shows learned addresses, not port settings.
whyWrong.2: `show ip interface brief` shows IP and interface state, not VLAN settings.
whyWrong.3: `show power inline` shows PoE data only.

exhibit.title: SW1# show interfaces fa0/7 switchport — excerpt
exhibit.text:
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 10 (USERS)
Voice VLAN: 30 (Inactive)

prompt: The port is meant to provide data VLAN 10 and voice VLAN 30. What switch-side defect does the output show?
options: The phone is proven to have registered in the data VLAN
The data VLAN is inactive because the voice VLAN is missing
The configured voice VLAN is inactive on this switch
The port must be a trunk because a voice VLAN is configured
explanation: The switchport output shows the configured voice VLAN as inactive. Restore it in the VLAN database, then check the phone’s power, provisioning and IP state.

whyWrong.0: The output does not show whether the phone registered.
whyWrong.1: The excerpt shows the voice VLAN inactive, not the data VLAN.
whyWrong.3: Access-plus-voice does not need a trunk.

prompt: Which statement about VLAN 1 is accurate for the Catalyst lab defaults?
options: Its existence means the switch already has secure remote management
It is the factory-default data access VLAN on this lab switch
It automatically routes packets between newly created VLANs
It is deleted automatically when another access VLAN is created
explanation: VLAN 1 is the factory-default access VLAN on the lab switch. Its existence gives no routing, remote management or security.

whyWrong.0: A VLAN does not create an IP address, SSH service or authentication.
whyWrong.2: A VLAN is Layer 2 and does not route between VLANs.
whyWrong.3: Creating another VLAN does not delete VLAN 1.

exhibit.title: SW1# show vlan brief — excerpt
exhibit.text:
10 USERS    active Fa0/1
20 PRINTERS active Fa0/2

prompt: PC-A is 192.168.10.11/24 on Fa0/1; PC-B is 192.168.10.12/24 on Fa0/2. Both links are up, and no routing or VLAN translation is configured. Why can they not communicate?
options: Their host addresses belong to different IPv4 subnets
The peers occupy different Layer 2 broadcast domains
The switch needs a management IP to learn either MAC address
Their default gateways must forward the same-subnet ARP request
explanation: The two ports are in different VLANs, so they are in different Layer 2 broadcast domains and ARP never reaches the peer. Fix the VLAN membership; a gateway does not bridge them.

whyWrong.2: Layer 2 forwarding needs no switch management IP.
whyWrong.3: The hosts treat each other as local, so no gateway is involved.

exhibit.title: Supplied relevant verification notes
exhibit.text:
SW1 Fa0/4:
 Administrative Mode: static access
 Operational Mode: static access
 Access Mode VLAN: 20 (Inactive)
Complete VLAN database check: VLAN 20 is absent.

prompt: A printer’s address and cable have not changed. Which correction addresses the condition shown for its data VLAN?
options: Recreate the intended VLAN 20 in the VLAN database
Move the printer to VLAN 1 while retaining its address
Change the switch management gateway to the printer
Clear learned MAC entries while leaving VLAN 20 absent
explanation: The port is assigned to VLAN 20, but VLAN 20 is missing and inactive. Recreate it in the VLAN database and keep the host address unchanged.

whyWrong.1: Moving the port changes the intended membership instead of restoring the VLAN.
whyWrong.2: A management gateway cannot create a VLAN.
whyWrong.3: Clearing MAC entries does not recreate a missing VLAN.

prompt: A phone is provisioned to tag voice traffic with VLAN 30. Its attached PC sends ordinary untagged data. The switchport has access VLAN 10 and voice VLAN 30. How are those two traffic types classified?
options: Both traffic types enter VLAN 30 because the phone is the physical neighbor
PC data enters VLAN 30; tagged voice enters VLAN 10
PC data enters VLAN 10; tagged voice enters VLAN 30
Both traffic types enter VLAN 10 because the port remains access mode
explanation: Untagged PC traffic uses the access VLAN (10), and tagged voice from the phone uses the voice VLAN (30).

whyWrong.0: The access VLAN still classifies the PC’s untagged data.
whyWrong.3: A voice VLAN lets an access port carry tagged voice in its own VLAN.

prompt: An AP requires 25 W available at the powered device. Considering the standard limits below, what is the lowest listed PoE standard that can supply it?
options: IEEE 802.3at, with up to 25.5 W available at the PD
IEEE 802.3af, with up to 12.95 W available at the PD
IEEE 802.3bt Type 3, as the first standard above 25 W at the PD
IEEE 802.3bt Type 4, as the first standard above 25 W at the PD
explanation: Compare power at the device, not at the switch port. 802.3at gives up to 25.5 W at the PD, which meets 25 W.

whyWrong.1: 802.3af gives only 12.95 W at the PD.
whyWrong.2: Type 3 supplies more, but 802.3at already meets the need.
whyWrong.3: Type 4 is not the lowest standard that meets 25 W.

prompt: A switch has a usable 370 W PoE allocation budget and 24 powered ports. Ten phones reserve 6.3 W each. Each additional AP requires 30 W of allocation at the PSE. How many APs fit within the remaining power and port capacity?
options: 9 APs, because every phone reserves a full 15.4 W
11 APs, because 307 divided by 30 rounds to eleven
14 APs, because fourteen physical ports remain free
10 APs, using 300 W of the remaining 307 W
explanation: Ten phones reserve 63 W, leaving 307 W. Ten 30 W APs need 300 W, and an eleventh would need 330 W.

whyWrong.0: The problem gives 6.3 W per phone, not 15.4 W.
whyWrong.1: Round down: eleven APs would exceed 307 W.
whyWrong.2: Free ports do not override the shared power budget.

exhibit.title: PoE allocation evidence — representative excerpt
exhibit.text:
Available: 370.0 W
Allocated: 345.0 W
Remaining:  25.0 W
Requested allocation on Gi1/0/13: 30.0 W
Operational state: power-deny

prompt: A compatible AP requests 30 W of PSE allocation on a port whose configured maximum is 30 W. Its cable and hardware capability pass checks. What best explains the denial shown?
options: The 30 W per-port maximum is below the 30 W request
The known-good cable cannot carry the supported PoE allocation
The shared budget has only 25 W remaining for a 30 W request
The AP has no assigned IP address before power negotiation
explanation: The port’s 30 W maximum matches the request, but the shared budget has only 25 W left. The shared budget is what denies the request.

whyWrong.0: The per-port maximum equals the 30 W request.
whyWrong.1: The scenario confirms the cable is fine.
whyWrong.3: PoE negotiation needs no IP address.

prompt: A virtual host presents tagged traffic for several VLANs over one physical uplink. Which connectivity choice fits that requirement?
options: A single access VLAN selected from the host’s management address
A voice-VLAN command for each of the virtual machines
An unconfigured port chosen only because its speed matches
A trunk with VLAN tagging and an allowed list matching the host
explanation: Several tagged VLANs on one uplink need trunking with tagging at both ends and an allowed list that matches the host. Chapter 10 covers the configuration.

whyWrong.0: One access VLAN cannot carry several tagged VLANs.
whyWrong.1: The voice VLAN feature is not a VM VLAN list.
whyWrong.2: Matching speed does not provide VLAN tagging.

prompt: An AP’s design uses one untagged management VLAN; client traffic is tunneled to its controller rather than locally presented as separate VLANs. Which port choice fits the stated uplink?
options: An access port in the AP management VLAN, with suitable power
A trunk whose native VLAN is chosen from a wireless client subnet
A voice port with the AP management VLAN used as voice VLAN
A routed port that removes the AP’s Layer 2 management VLAN
explanation: This AP presents one untagged management VLAN and tunnels client traffic to the controller, so an access port in the AP management VLAN with suitable power fits.

whyWrong.1: The AP presents only its untagged management network, not a client-subnet native VLAN.
whyWrong.2: The voice VLAN feature is for phones, not AP management.
whyWrong.3: A routed port removes the Layer 2 attachment the AP uses.

prompt: Which endpoint needs extra care before you reuse a single-PC access-port design?
options: A single printer specified to send one untagged data network
A single workstation with one untagged Ethernet interface
A standalone sensor specified to use one untagged data VLAN
A transparent firewall that bridges frames from other devices
explanation: A transparent firewall bridges frames from other devices, so its port can carry many source MACs and a wider Layer 2 path. Check its role before applying edge protections.

whyWrong.0: A printer sending one untagged network fits a normal access port.
whyWrong.1: A single workstation fits the basic host-port example.
whyWrong.2: A sensor on one untagged VLAN fits a normal access port.

prompt: After erasing startup configuration on a Catalyst switch, normal-range user VLANs are still present. Which two statements explain how to verify this? Choose two.
options: VLAN information can persist in the separate VLAN database
Erasing startup configuration guarantees deletion of every switch file
The name of a VLAN determines whether it is stored persistently
A remaining VLAN proves a router is still forwarding between subnets
Check VLAN definitions and interface assignments separately
explanation: VLAN definitions can persist in a separate VLAN database, so erasing startup-config may not remove them. Check VLAN definitions and port assignments separately.

whyWrong.1: Erasing startup-config does not delete every file on the switch.
whyWrong.2: A VLAN’s name does not decide whether it persists.
whyWrong.3: A VLAN entry says nothing about routing.

prompt: An untagged printer must join existing active VLAN 50 on unused Fa0/8. The port is enabled. Which interface configuration implements that requirement?
options: `switchport mode trunk` and `switchport trunk allowed vlan 50`
`switchport mode access` and `switchport voice vlan 50`
`switchport mode access` and `switchport access vlan 50`
`switchport mode access` and `switchport access vlan 1`
explanation: `switchport mode access` fixes static access mode, and `switchport access vlan 50` sets the data VLAN.

whyWrong.0: A trunk is not an ordinary single-VLAN endpoint attachment.
whyWrong.1: The voice VLAN command does not set the data VLAN.
whyWrong.3: This assigns VLAN 1, not VLAN 50.

exhibit.title: Representative PoE configuration and state
exhibit.text:
Interface Gi1/0/7
 power inline never
Verified per-port capability: sufficient for this endpoint
Shared remaining allocation: sufficient
Observed endpoint power: off

prompt: The endpoint and cable work on a second PoE port, and this port has enough power and budget. Which change fixes the displayed administrative condition?
options: Set `power inline auto` on the intended supported interface
Assign the port to the endpoint's untagged data VLAN
Clear its dynamic MAC entries before retrying power
Add a management address to the switch's existing VLAN
explanation: The port is administratively blocked from supplying PoE. `power inline auto` restores automatic detection.

whyWrong.1: VLAN membership does not enable PoE.
whyWrong.2: Clearing MAC entries does not enable PoE detection.
whyWrong.3: PoE discovery needs no management address.

prompt: An ordinary PC must use a fixed access port in existing VLAN 10. The port operates as access but its administrative mode is dynamic auto. Which change completes the stated mode requirement?
options: Set `switchport voice vlan 10` and leave the administrative mode
Set `switchport mode trunk` while retaining VLAN 10
Set `switchport access vlan 10` again while retaining dynamic auto
Set `switchport mode access` while retaining access VLAN 10
explanation: A port in dynamic auto can operate as access without being fixed in static access mode. `switchport mode access` sets the administrative mode.

whyWrong.0: The voice VLAN does not set static access mode.
whyWrong.1: A trunk does not meet the fixed access requirement.
whyWrong.2: The access VLAN is already right and does not change the mode.

prompt: A replacement IoT sensor sends one untagged data network and needs PoE. Its static access port is in VLAN 10 with power disabled, and VLAN 60 is correct. Which two changes meet the requirement?
options: `switchport voice vlan 60`
`power inline never`
`switchport access vlan 60`
`switchport access vlan 10`
`power inline auto`
explanation: Set the access VLAN to 60 and enable PoE with `power inline auto`. The existing static access mode can stay.

whyWrong.0: A sensor needs a data access VLAN, not a voice VLAN.
whyWrong.3: VLAN 10 is the wrong VLAN.

exhibit.title: Supplied voice/data checks
exhibit.text:
Fa0/7 operational access VLAN 10, voice VLAN 30
VLANs 10 and 30 active
Phone power on; phone IPv4 address 0.0.0.0
PC data test to VLAN 10 peer succeeds

prompt: The attached PC communicates normally. The powered phone's voice VLAN is active, but its displayed IPv4 address is 0.0.0.0; its design requires automatic addressing. What should be checked next before changing switchport mode?
options: Whether the working PC can still use its existing data-VLAN address
Whether the phone's required voice addressing and provisioning service is available
Whether changing both data and voice to VLAN 10 permits the phone to boot
Whether clearing the PC's MAC entry makes the switch assign the phone an IP
explanation: Power and the voice VLAN are fine, but the phone has no address. Check the voice network’s addressing and provisioning service, because the working PC proves nothing about it.

whyWrong.0: Retesting the PC does not test voice address acquisition.
whyWrong.2: Moving voice to VLAN 10 abandons the voice design without finding the missing service.
whyWrong.3: The MAC table does not supply IP configuration.

exhibit.title: Supplied endpoint and switch evidence
exhibit.text:
Documented LAN: VLAN 40, 192.168.40.0/24
PC-A: 192.168.40.10/24, no gateway, Fa0/1
PC-B: 192.168.41.20/24, no gateway, Fa0/2
Fa0/1 and Fa0/2: connected; static access VLAN 40
VLAN 40: active; fresh A and B MAC entries in VLAN 40

prompt: Both PCs use the same active VLAN and their source MACs are learned on the expected ports. No router or gateway is configured. Which correction addresses the documented inconsistency?
options: Move PC-B's port to a new VLAN named after its current address
Give PC-B an unused address in the documented 192.168.40.0/24 LAN
Create a switch management SVI using PC-B's current address
Change only PC-A's mask to /16 while leaving PC-B at /24
explanation: The VLAN membership is correct, but PC-B’s address is in another subnet, and there is no router. Give PC-B an unused address in 192.168.40.0/24, such as .20.

whyWrong.0: Moving the port breaks the shared VLAN and adds no routing.
whyWrong.2: A management address does not fix PC-B’s subnet.
whyWrong.3: A mismatched mask makes the hosts disagree about what is local.

prompt: An AP needs a supported 30 W allocation at the PSE. All listed PoE ports and cabling support its negotiation method. Which unused port meets both the per-port and shared-budget constraints?
options: SW-A: per-port maximum 15.4 W; shared remaining 60 W
SW-B: per-port maximum 30 W; shared remaining 25 W
SW-C: per-port maximum 30 W; shared remaining 40 W
SW-D: per-port maximum 20 W; shared remaining 80 W
explanation: The AP needs a 30 W per-port limit and at least 30 W of shared budget. Only SW-C meets both.

whyWrong.0: SW-A’s 15.4 W per-port maximum is below 30 W.
whyWrong.1: SW-B has only 25 W of shared budget left.
whyWrong.3: SW-D’s 20 W per-port maximum is below 30 W.

prompt: Which VLAN ID range is the normal range on the Catalyst platforms used here?
explanation: Normal-range VLANs are 1–1005. Extended-range VLANs are 1006–4094.

whyWrong.1: 1–4094 is the full usable range, normal plus extended.
whyWrong.3: VLAN 0 and 4095 are not ordinary configurable VLANs.

prompt: A data VLAN is deleted while access ports are still assigned to it. What happens to those ports?
options: They go inactive and do not return to VLAN 1
They move back into VLAN 1 automatically
They become trunk ports automatically
They join the native VLAN instead
explanation: Ports whose VLAN is deleted go inactive. They are not moved back to VLAN 1.

whyWrong.1: A deleted VLAN does not automatically move ports to VLAN 1.
whyWrong.2: Deleting a VLAN does not change a port’s mode.
whyWrong.3: Access ports do not join a native VLAN when their VLAN is deleted.

prompt: Which statement about VLAN 1 is true?
options: Every port starts in it, and it cannot be deleted
It can be deleted once another VLAN exists
It is the extended-range VLAN
Ports start in it only after a reload
explanation: VLAN 1 is the default VLAN: every port starts in it, and it cannot be deleted or renamed.

whyWrong.1: VLAN 1 cannot be deleted at all.
whyWrong.2: VLAN 1 is in the normal range, 1–1005.
whyWrong.3: Ports begin in VLAN 1 by default, with no reload needed.

prompt: Which interface command sets a port’s data VLAN to 10?
options: switchport access vlan 10
switchport mode access
switchport voice vlan 10
switchport trunk native vlan 10
explanation: `switchport access vlan 10` sets the data VLAN. `switchport mode access` is a separate command that fixes the port’s mode.

whyWrong.1: `switchport mode access` fixes the mode but sets no VLAN.
whyWrong.2: `switchport voice vlan 10` sets the voice VLAN.
whyWrong.3: That sets a trunk’s native VLAN, not an access VLAN.
